key_insight: 2D Gum-Net learns dense elastic image alignment without ground-truth deformation fields, improving fingerprint structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004.
clinical_relevance: The approach may inform medical image registration where deformation labels are scarce, but the reported evaluation is on fingerprints rather than clinical images.
method: Adapts 3D Gum-Net to 2D registration using symmetric correlation.
Predicts a sparse control-point grid and uses bicubic interpolation to produce dense deformation fields.
Uses DCT spectral pooling to preserve fine patterns, with frozen-basis matrix operations reporting approximately 50× GPU speedup.
evidence_signal: Trained solely on synthetic fingerprint impressions and tested zero-shot on real benchmarks, the model improved structural correlation and independent-matcher genuine scores while leaving impostor scores essentially unchanged.
watch_item: Generalization to clinical imaging and anatomical validity of predicted deformations remain unestablished by the fingerprint evaluation.
paper_title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
